## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kusanāḷijātaka* (Ja 121) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The frame story (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivered the teaching concerning a loyal friend of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Anāthapiṇḍika’s relatives and associates urged him to terminate the friendship because the companion was neither his equal nor his superior in birth or wealth, but Anāthapiṇḍika maintained that true friendship does not depend on outward status or social equality [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].

In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was reborn as a lowly spirit dwelling in a clump of *kusa* grass (*kusanāḷigacche devatā*) and befriended a deity residing in an adjoining royal tree (*rucādevatā*) [Sahni 2008; Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. When the king's builders sought to fell the beautiful tree to make a supporting pillar for the palace, the Bodhisatta managed to save the tree deity's dwelling [Sahni 2008; Anandajoti 2010]. In praise of their bond, the tree deity proclaimed the story's canonical verse (*Kare sarikkho athavāpi seṭṭho...*), declaring that whether a friend is an equal, a superior, or of lower standing, any wise friend may provide the greatest benefit in times of misfortune [Fausböll 1877; Anandajoti 2010]. In the narrative's conclusion (*samodhāna*), the tree deity is identified as Ānanda and the grass deity as the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1877].

The text was edited by V. Fausböll in his edition of the Jātaka commentary [Fausböll 1877]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. No internal Pali text reuses or cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or greater are detected by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus], and no curated parallels are registered on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
